Background The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Mongolia Country Office supports the Government of Mongolia in achieving sustainable development outcomes in line with national priorities and the UNDP Country Programme. UNDP Mongolia places particular emphasis on integrated approaches to climate action, environmental sustainability, and inclusive governance. Within this framework, UNDP implements the Climate Adaptation and Sustainable Management of Natural Ecosystems Portfolio, which aims to strengthen climate resilience, promote low-emission development pathways, improve ecosystem management, and enhance institutional, policy, and financing mechanisms at national and subnational levels. The Green and Inclusive Cities in Mongolia Project is a new national initiative implemented by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MECC) with technical and implementation support from UNDP, with the overall goal to support the transition toward integrated, inclusive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient urban development by strengthening urban planning and governance systems, improving cross-sectoral coordination, advancing results-based green budgeting and public finance, piloting inclusive and climate-responsive urban solutions, and enhancing institutional and human capacities at national and municipal levels. The project addresses critical environmental, social, and climate-related challenges arising from rapid urbanization and is implemented in Ulaanbaatar, Darkhan, and Erdenet cities. A central pillar of the project is transforming how cities plan, finance, and deliver development — strengthening municipal financial management and expanding access to innovative financing instruments such as blended finance, public–private partnerships (PPPs), and green municipal bonds to mobilize capital for low-carbon heating, clean transportation, flood protection, energy-efficient buildings, sustainable mobility, and ecological restoration. Against this background, the Green Finance Expert will lead the design and roll-out of innovative and sustainable financing solutions and strengthen the capacity of national and municipal institutions and development finance partners to structure, raise, and manage such finance. The project is implemented through a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) under the oversight of a Project National Coordinator and in close coordination with national government and municipal counterparts. The incumbent shall work in close collaboration with the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) staff and the Consultants’ Team of the project, and in collaboration with UNDP’s sustainable-finance projects and teams. Conduct financial feasibility, structuring, and de-risking analyses for priority green investments (e.g., low-carbon heating, clean transportation, flood protection, energy efficiency, and ecological restoration, agroforestry, organic food supply-chain), including cash-flow modelling, bankability assessment, and identification of revenue and repayment streams; Conduct risk, scenario, and stress-testing analysis of financing structures - including macro-fiscal and debt-sustainability considerations - and propose appropriate risk-mitigation and risk-sharing arrangements; Develop green urban investment pipelines and financing roadmaps for Ulaanbaatar, Darkhan, and Erdenet, prioritizing projects against climate, biodiversity, social-inclusion, and financial criteria; Advise on the enabling policy, regulatory, and market conditions required to deploy green and innovative financing instruments at the municipal level; Pilot a green and inclusive municipal tax reform in Darkhan, including green levies or modified taxes with affordability and distributional safeguards for low-income households; Support the establishment or strengthening of a city/aimag sustainable development fund or investment corporation in Darkhan and Erdenet, with transparent governance, fiduciary controls, and a bankable project pipeline; Prepare an Ulaanbaatar Green Municipal Bond feasibility study and issuance roadmap - covering revenue streams, investor demand, legal readiness, and regulatory compliance - extendable to Darkhan and Erdenet as the legal framework allows; Support PPP structuring and revenue-earning service models in priority sectors (food-safety labs, water systems, waste logistics, park operations), using blended-finance models that combine public funds, concessional loans, and risk-sharing instruments; In coordination with the Renewable Energy Expert, design and test tailored financial instruments (interest-rate buy-downs, green mortgages, results-based subsidies, credit guarantees, and PPP frameworks) to scale up low-emission energy investments, with affordability and gender-responsive access assessments. Strengthen Municipal Public Financial Management (PFM) And Own-source Revenue Assess municipal PFM systems (planning, budgeting, execution, revenue administration, accounting, and reporting) and identify entry points to integrate climate, green, and biodiversity considerations, including results-based green budgeting and green budget tagging; Support the strengthening and diversification of municipal own-source revenue, including land- and property-based instruments, user charges and tariffs, and land-value capture, to improve creditworthiness and fiscal space for green investment; Advise on aligning municipal capital investment planning and budgeting with green and climate priorities and integrating financing strategies into cities’ medium-term fiscal frameworks and urban development plans; Support the development of municipal creditworthiness and financial-sustainability improvement plans as a basis for accessing market-based and development finance; Implement green and climate-supportive Medium-Term Budget Frameworks and results-based green budgeting in the three cities, linking Green City indicators to planning, expenditure tagging, IFMIS, and INFF; Develop and apply an Impact Measurement and Management (IMM) framework for the biodiversity, climate, environmental, and social co-benefits of municipal investments, to support access to green finance and green bonds; Support public financial management reform enabling blended finance and inclusive oversight, aligned with decentralization; Strengthen institutional capacity for carbon finance (e.g., Verra, Gold Standard, MRV) and expand urban carbon-market readiness. Engage Development Banks And Mobilize Institutional Engagement Engage national and international development banks, development finance institutions (DFIs), climate funds, and other institutional financiers to identify and structure co-financing and lending opportunities for green urban projects; Advise on the design or strengthening of financing vehicles and intermediation arrangements (e.g., project preparation facilities, on-lending, and credit-enhancement structures) that channel development finance to municipal and green urban investments; Assess the eligibility, appraisal, and safeguard requirements of relevant development banks and climate funds, and support the preparation of project concepts and applications that meet these standards; Facilitate technical dialogue between municipalities, MECC, and development finance partners to align pipelines, instruments, and timelines. Build Financing-sector Partnerships And Private-sector Engagement Map and engage financial-sector stakeholders — commercial banks, the central bank and financial regulators, capital-market institutions, institutional investors, insurers, and green/sustainable finance associations — to build partnerships for green urban finance; Support the design of public–private partnerships (PPPs) and private-sector engagement models for green urban infrastructure and services, including risk-sharing and revenue arrangements; Promote the uptake of sustainable-finance standards, taxonomies, and disclosure practices (e.g., green bond frameworks, second-party opinions, use-of-proceeds and impact reporting) among partner institutions; Organize and facilitate roundtables, investor dialogues, and matchmaking events connecting municipalities and project sponsors with prospective financiers. Lead Resource Mobilization And Fundraising Develop and implement a resource-mobilization strategy to raise public, private, philanthropic, and blended capital for the project’s green and inclusive urban investments; Prepare high-quality investment cases, pitch materials, concept notes, and funding proposals for submission to donors, climate funds, development banks, and private investors; Identify and track funding opportunities and calls, and coordinate the preparation and timely submission of competitive applications; Establish systems to monitor, report, and communicate financing results, including capital mobilized (public, private, and co-financing leverage ratios) and associated climate, environmental, and social outcomes. The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange. Business Management Working with Evidence and Data: Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies Project Management: Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocol
